title: $LONG^2RAG$: Evaluating Long-Context \& Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Key Point Recall
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: LONG2RAG benchmark with Key Point Recall (KPR) metric for evaluating long-context, long-form RAG. Explicitly motivates by low signal-to-noise ratio and dispersed information in retrieved docs, and reports degradation as input docs grow (long-context distraction-like effect). Main contribution is evaluation protocol rather than a robustness mechanism; supports robust-RAG positioning as a benchmark resource.

title: A Hybrid Retrieval Approach for Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Natural Language and Speech Processing (ICNLSP 2024)
notes: General RAG application proposing a hybrid retriever combining text embeddings and knowledge-graph embeddings to improve retrieval accuracy in a health-tech use case. While it briefly motivates the work via 'false retrieval', the contribution is a retrieval-quality method, not a robustness, unreliable-evidence, adversarial, calibration, or answerability analysis. Out of scope for Map B.

title: Accelerating Inference of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Sparse Context Selection
authors: Yun Zhu; Jia-Chen Gu; Caitlin Sikora; Ho Ko; Yinxiao Liu; Chu-Cheng Lin; Lei Shu; Liangchen Luo; Lei Meng; Bang Liu; Jindong Chen
notes: Primary contribution is inference acceleration via sparse context selection (sparse KV-cache decoding), not robustness to unreliable evidence. The per-context assessment is in service of efficiency, though it incidentally filters irrelevant docs (touches noisy_retrieval and adaptive control). No threat model, no faithfulness/calibration evaluation, no robustness benchmark. Boundary context only.

title: AceSearcher: Bootstrapping Reasoning and Search for LLMs via Reinforced Self-Play
authors: Ran Xu; Yuchen Zhuang; Zihan Dong; Ruiyu Wang; Yue Yu; Joyce C. Ho; Linjun Zhang; Haoyu Wang; Wenqi Shi; Carl Yang
notes: Self-play RL training framework for multi-hop search-augmented LLMs via decomposer/solver roles. Focus is on improving reasoning and search effectiveness for complex QA, not on handling unreliable evidence, noisy retrieval, adversarial inputs, knowledge conflicts, or answerability. General RAG capability enhancement; closest taxonomy fit is calibration_control via adaptive decomposition-driven retrieval, but no robustness or evidence-quality analysis.

title: Attention in Large Language Models Yields Efficient Zero-Shot Re-Rankers
authors: Shijie Chen; Bernal Jimenez Gutierrez; Yu Su
notes: Proposes in-context re-ranking (ICR) leveraging LLM attention weights for efficient zero-shot re-ranking. Focus is on efficiency and quality of re-ranking, not on robustness to unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflicts, or selective prediction. Mentions calibration but only to mitigate attention biases (content-free query), not for abstention/control. Closest label is noisy_retrieval as better re-ranking reduces noisy context, but no explicit robustness contribution; treat as background/boundary.

title: BSharedRAG: Backbone Shared Retrieval-Augmented Generation for the E-commerce Domain
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Domain-specific RAG framework for e-commerce using a shared LLM backbone with two LoRA modules for retrieval and generation. Contribution is architectural (parameter sharing, negative transfer avoidance, hard negative mining) and dataset construction (WorthBuying). Although the motivation mentions noisy/conflicting user-generated reviews and hallucinations, the paper does not analyze, evaluate, or mitigate retrieval noise, distraction, conflict, or adversarial conditions as a robustness contribution. General RAG method paper, not robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence.

title: Boosting the Potential of Large Language Models with an Intelligent Information Assistant
authors: Yujia Zhou; Zheng Liu; Zhicheng Dou
notes: AssistRAG is a general RAG enhancement framework with an intelligent assistant module for memory/knowledge management. While it includes plan-specification decisions ('Is Memory Useful?' / 'Is Knowledge Useful?') that touch on calibration/control, the primary contribution is improving complex reasoning QA performance via a trainable assistant plugin, not robustness under unreliable evidence. No explicit treatment of noisy retrieval, conflicts, attacks, or answerability. Borderline boundary context only.

title: BordIRlines: A Dataset for Evaluating Cross-lingual Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Advancing Natural Language Processing for Wikipedia
notes: Introduces BordIRlines dataset for evaluating robustness of cross-lingual RAG on geopolitical disputes. Tests consistency under conflicting multilingual evidence; primary contribution is benchmark/dataset, with knowledge_conflict as the underlying failure mode (different language sources give different perspectives). Workshop paper at ACL.

title: C-3PO: Compact Plug-and-Play Proxy Optimization to Achieve Human-like Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors:
Guoxin Chen, Minpeng Liao, Peiying Yu, Dingmin Wang, Zile Qiao, Chao Yang, Xin Zhao, Kai Fan;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:8530-8551
notes: ICML 2025 proxy-centric multi-agent framework for RAG. Three agents handle: (1) Reasoning Router decides retrieval necessity and complexity (adaptive/selective retrieval), (2) Information Filter selects relevant docs (noise filtering), (3) Decision Maker assesses sufficiency to answer or continue retrieving. Core contribution is calibrated control over when/what to retrieve and what evidence to trust. Tested on OOD datasets including FreshQA and MultiHop-RAG. Borderline robust-RAG paper—primary focus is alignment/performance, but the adaptive retrieval gating and information filtering meaningfully address calibration_control and noisy_retrieval. Includes as support.

title: Can Knowledge-Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation Really Retrieve What You Need?
authors: Junchi Yu; Yujie Liu; Jindong Gu; Philip Torr; Dongzhan Zhou
notes: Proposes GraphFlow, a GFlowNet-style framework for KG-based RAG that retrieves accurate and diverse knowledge for complex queries via flow estimator + retrieval policy. Contribution is a general retrieval method improvement for complex multi-step KG queries (accuracy + diversity), not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, noise, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibration. Mentions robustness/generalization to unseen KGs only briefly. Closest taxonomy match is noisy_retrieval as it concerns retrieval imperfection, but it does not explicitly evaluate/mitigate noise. Out of scope.

title: Chunk-Distilled Language Modeling
authors: Yanhong Li; Karen Livescu; Jiawei Zhou
notes: CD-LM is a training-free chunk-level retrieval-augmented decoding method aimed at inference efficiency and knowledge adaptation (distillation/domain adaptation). It does not address unreliable evidence, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflicts, calibration, abstention, or robustness evaluation. General RAG/efficiency contribution; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Context Tuning for Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Uncertainty-Aware NLP (UncertaiNLP 2024)
notes: Paper proposes 'Context Tuning' to improve tool retrieval for underspecified/implicit queries in agentic RAG, using LambdaMART+RRF with usage signals. Although the venue is UncertaiNLP and the paper briefly mentions hallucination reduction, the core contribution is a retrieval-engineering method for tool selection, not analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, robustness perturbations, calibration, or adversarial conditions. Closest taxonomy fit is ood_uncertainty (implicit queries) but contribution is general RAG improvement, so excluded from map.

title: Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Question Answering: Mutual Information Exchange and Ranking by Contrasting Layers
authors: Youmin Ko; Sung Jong Seo; Hyunjoon Kim
notes: CoopRAG proposes a cooperative RAG framework combining question unrolling (with uncertainty masking), unrolling-augmented retrieval, contrastive layer reranking, and reasoning chain completion for single/multi-hop QA. While it touches on incorrect retrievals and LLM uncertainty, the main contribution is a general RAG architecture aimed at improving retrieval and QA accuracy rather than a focused study of unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, calibration, or evaluation of robustness. Boundary case; primary lab noisy_retrieval as closest fit.

title: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: EMG-RAG is a personalized RAG application using editable memory graphs and RL-based adaptive memory selection for smartphone AI assistants. While it uses adaptive selection (loose connection to calibration_control) and briefly mentions noise from irrelevant memories, the core contribution is personalization, memory management, and end-to-end optimization, not robustness under unreliable evidence, adversarial attacks, knowledge conflicts, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: DSLR: Document Refinement with Sentence-Level Re-ranking and Reconstruction to Enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 3rd Workshop on Knowledge Augmented Methods for NLP
notes: DSLR decomposes retrieved passages into sentences, re-ranks them, and reconstructs coherent passages to filter out irrelevant/redundant info that distracts LLMs. Explicit mitigation for retrieval noise and distractor content in RAG context. Workshop paper at KnowledgeNLP@ACL 2024.

title: EAReranker: Efficient Embedding Adequacy Assessment for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Dongyang Zeng; Yaping Liu; Wei Zhang; Shuo Zhang; Xinwang Liu; Binxing Fang
notes: Efficient embedding-based reranker that scores document 'adequacy' (verifiability, coverage, completeness, structure) instead of pure relevance, claiming to filter inadequate docs that could mislead RAG. However, the paper's primary contributions are computational efficiency (constant memory, 2-3x faster) and privacy (no plaintext access), not analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, distractors, conflicts, or adversarial corruption. Borderline case; closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval since it filters low-utility docs, but framing is general reranking improvement rather than a robustness-under-unreliable-evidence contribution.

title: Entity-Focused Dense Passage Retrieval for Outside-Knowledge Visual Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Multimodal RAG retrieval improvement for OK-VQA via entity-focused dense passage retrieval. Although the paper notes retrieved knowledge is often inadequate/too general (weak supervision), the contribution is a better retriever for VQA, not robustness analysis, mitigation of unreliable evidence, calibration, conflict handling, or adversarial defense. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: FiD-Light: Efficient and Effective Retrieval-Augmented Text Generation
authors: Sebastian Hofstätter; Jiecao Chen; Karthik Raman; Hamed Zamani
notes: FiD-Light focuses on efficiency-effectiveness tradeoff in retrieval-augmented generation via compressing encoder-decoder information flow and adding source-pointer re-ranking. Evaluated on KILT for combined text generation + provenance precision. While it briefly discusses robustness of source pointers to distribution shifts in #relevant passages, the main contribution is efficiency, not unreliable evidence, conflict, adversarial, or calibration. Background only.

title: Graph-KV: Breaking Sequence via Injecting Structural Biases into Large Language Models
authors: Haoyu Peter Wang; Peihao Wang; Mufei Li; Shikun Liu; Siqi Miao; Zhangyang Wang; Pan Li
notes: Graph-KV is primarily an architectural/efficiency contribution that modifies KV-cache attention to inject structural inductive biases for RAG and graph-structured data. It reduces positional bias and supports parallel encoding of retrieved chunks, with evaluation on RAG/multi-hop benchmarks. While it touches positional bias and notes noisy multi-hop reasoning, the central contribution is structural encoding/efficiency rather than analyzing or mitigating unreliable evidence (no retrieval noise, conflict, attack, abstention, or answerability analysis). Closest taxonomy fit is distraction (positional bias/context utilization), but out of map scope.

title: Hierarchical Planning for Complex Tasks with Knowledge Graph-RAG and Symbolic Verification
authors:
Flavio Petruzzellis, Cristina Cornelio, Pietro Lio;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:49105-49127
notes: Paper integrates KG-based RAG with hierarchical planning and a symbolic validator for robotic task planning. RAG is a knowledge source component, not the subject of robustness analysis. Symbolic verifier addresses plan correctness/failure detection (an agentic control mechanism) rather than unreliable retrieval evidence (noise, conflict, attack, ambiguity). Primary contribution is neuro-symbolic agentic planning; closest taxonomy fit is multimodal_agentic_code but the paper is not centered on RAG robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: Holistic Reasoning with Long-Context LMs: A Benchmark for Database Operations on Massive Textual Data
authors: Seiji Maekawa; Hayate Iso; Nikita Bhutani
notes: HoloBench is a long-context LM benchmark testing holistic/aggregation reasoning by mixing relevant and irrelevant verbalized DB rows; it discusses RAG limitations and controls information density/position (distraction-adjacent). However, the main contribution is evaluating LCLM capabilities, not robustness of RAG under unreliable evidence. Boundary/background context only.

title: HyPA-RAG: A Hybrid Parameter Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for AI Legal and Policy Applications
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Customizable NLP: Progress and Challenges in Customizing NLP for a Domain, Application, Group, or Individual (CustomNLP4U)
notes: Domain-specific legal/policy RAG system (NYC LL144) featuring a query complexity classifier for adaptive parameter tuning, hybrid (dense/sparse/KG) retrieval, and a custom RAGAS-style evaluation framework. While it mentions common RAG failure points and includes some adaptive-control flavor, the contribution is primarily an application-oriented system with domain evaluation, not a robustness-to-unreliable-evidence study. Closest taxonomy hook is calibration_control (query-conditioned parameter adaptation), with secondary evaluation_benchmark for the custom question types and metrics.

title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yiqun Chen; Lingyong Yan; Weiwei Sun; Xinyu Ma; Yi Zhang; Shuaiqiang Wang; Dawei Yin; Yiming Yang; Jiaxin Mao
notes: MMOA-RAG proposes multi-agent RL to jointly optimize a standard RAG pipeline (query rewriter, retriever, selector, generator) toward F1 reward. Although the selector module filters documents and the system arguably learns to use evidence, the paper's contribution is general end-to-end pipeline optimization, not robustness to unreliable evidence, noise, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibrated abstention. No explicit perturbation/noise/attack evaluation. Out of scope; closest taxonomy bucket is calibration_control via the selector + joint reward decisioning.

title: KnowGPT: Knowledge Graph based Prompting for Large Language Models
authors: Qinggang Zhang; Junnan Dong; Hao Chen; Daochen Zha; Zailiang Yu; Xiao Huang
notes: General GraphRAG/KG-prompting framework using deep RL for knowledge extraction and MAB for prompt construction. Main contributions target three issues: huge search space, high API cost, and laborious prompt design. While it briefly mentions data quality issues in motivation, the actual work is a standard KG-RAG QA method focused on efficiency and accuracy, not robustness to unreliable evidence, adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration. Out of scope.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Knowledge Graphs
authors: Minki Kang; Jin Myung Kwak; Jinheon Baek; Sung Ju Hwang
notes: KG-augmented dialogue generation (SURGE). Explicitly analyzes irrelevant retrieval (87% of 1-hop KG facts irrelevant) and proposes context-relevant subgraph retrieval plus graph-text contrastive learning to enforce faithfulness/consistency with retrieved knowledge. Addresses unreliable evidence (noisy KG facts) and hallucination, but in dialogue/KG setting rather than open-domain text RAG—hence support, not core.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
authors: Minki Kang; Jin Myung Kwak; Jinheon Baek; Sung Ju Hwang
notes: SURGE: KG-augmented dialogue generation that explicitly tackles irrelevant retrieval (87% of 1-hop facts are irrelevant) via GNN-based subgraph retrieval and addresses hallucination/faithfulness via graph-text contrastive learning. Introduces KQA metric for faithfulness evaluation. Borderline support: not framed as adversarial robustness, but addresses noisy retrieval and knowledge consistency as core contributions.

title: LI-RAGE: Late Interaction Retrieval Augmented Generation with Explicit Signals for Open-Domain Table Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 2: Short Papers)
notes: Open-domain TableQA method paper combining ColBERT late interaction retrieval, RAGE joint training, and a binary yes/no relevance token prefix to filter non-gold retrieved tables. The relevance-token mechanism has a tangential connection to deciding when retrieved evidence is reliable, but the paper's primary contribution is SOTA on NQ-TABLES and E2E-WTQ, not robustness under unreliable evidence, knowledge conflict, adversarial corruption, or systematic evaluation of noisy retrieval. General RAG application; exclude from map.

title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
authors: Gaurang Sriramanan; Siddhant Bharti; Vinu Sankar Sadasivan; Shoumik Saha; Priyatham Kattakinda; Soheil Feizi
notes: Proposes LLM-Check, a hallucination detection method using internal attention maps, hidden states, and output probabilities of an auxiliary LLM. Includes evaluation on RAGTruth (RAG-specific hallucination benchmark) where ground-truth references are available, making it relevant to detecting unreliable/ungrounded generation in RAG. Primary contribution is detection enabling trust decisions, hence calibration_control; secondary knowledge_conflict because RAG hallucinations often reflect conflict between parametric and retrieved evidence. Not a core RAG robustness paper but a useful supporting tool.

title: LLMs as Collaborator: Demands-Guided Collaborative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Commonsense Knowledge-Grounded Open-Domain Dialogue Systems
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Method paper proposing collaborative RAG (DCRAG) for commonsense knowledge-grounded dialogue. Focus is on better identifying retrieval demands via LLM-retriever collaboration to improve response quality. Mentions hallucination/outdated knowledge as motivation, but contribution is a general RAG improvement for dialogue, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence/security/calibration/conflict mechanism. Out of scope.

title: Lift Yourself Up: Retrieval-augmented Text Generation with Self-Memory
authors: Xin Cheng; Di Luo; Xiuying Chen; Lemao Liu; Dongyan Zhao; Rui Yan
notes: Selfmem proposes using model's own output as iterative self-memory to overcome fixed-corpus quality limitations in retrieval-augmented generation (MT, summarization, dialogue). Focuses on generation quality improvement via memory selection, not on robustness against unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflicts, calibration, or answerability. General RAG quality-enhancement method — out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: M-RAG: Reinforcing Large Language Model Performance through Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Multiple Partitions
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: M-RAG proposes a multi-partition paradigm with multi-agent RL (Agent-S for partition selection, Agent-R for memory refinement) to improve RAG performance on summarization, translation, and dialogue generation. While motivation briefly mentions noise from coarse-grained AKNN retrieval, the contribution is a general performance-improvement method, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence study. No adversarial, conflict, calibration, or evaluation-of-robustness contribution. Out of scope.

title: Modeling Uncertainty and Using Post-fusion as Fallback Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation with LLMs
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Language Models (KnowLLM 2024)
notes: Paper models LLM uncertainty via 'unknown' outputs and proposes post-fusion as fallback strategy when concatenation fails. Addresses calibration/fallback decisions (when to switch strategy) and distraction (LLM fails even when correct passage is in top-k under oracle setting). Multi-round feedback approaches. Workshop paper at KnowLLM 2024, useful support for robust RAG positioning.

title: Multi-Hop Paragraph Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
notes: MUPPET proposes an iterative multi-hop paragraph retrieval method for open-domain QA (SQuAD-Open, HotpotQA). It is a general retrieval/QA methodology paper without explicit analysis or mitigation of unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial threats, calibration, or evidence quality. Out of scope; closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval only by virtue of being a retrieval method.

title: Multi-Level Information Retrieval Augmented Generation for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Multimodal RAG method (MiRAG) for Knowledge-based VQA that introduces multi-level retrieval (entity + passage) with query expansion and end-to-end joint training. While the motivation briefly mentions noisy/pseudo-relevant retrieval signals, the main contribution is improving retrieval quality and answer accuracy on ViQuAE benchmark, not robustness under unreliable evidence, attacks, conflicts, calibration, or answerability. Standard multimodal RAG application; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Multi-Task Dense Retrieval via Model Uncertainty Fusion for Open-Domain Question Answering
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2021
notes: Multi-task DPR that uses ensemble model uncertainty (mutual information) to weight predictions from different domain-specific retrievers. 'Corpus inconsistency' here refers to training data overlap across QA datasets, not contradictions among retrieved evidence. Uncertainty is used for expert selection rather than for assessing evidence quality, abstention, or robustness against unreliable evidence. Closest taxonomy label is calibration_control because of the uncertainty-weighted fusion, but the contribution is about multi-task retrieval optimization, not robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Neural Graph Matching Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation in Molecular Machine Learning
authors:
Runzhong Wang, Rui-Xi Wang, Mrunali Manjrekar, Connor W. Coley;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:64734-64749
notes: Domain-specific RAG application for molecular mass spectrum simulation using neural graph matching. While it mentions noise-robust matching, this refers to robustness in graph affinity learning for molecular structures, not robustness of RAG under unreliable evidence. No contribution on retrieval noise analysis, conflicts, adversarial attacks, calibration, or robust RAG evaluation. Out of scope.

title: NutriBench: A Dataset for Evaluating Large Language Models in Nutrition Estimation from Meal Descriptions
authors: Mehak Preet Dhaliwal; Andong Hua; Laya Pullela; Ryan Burke; Yao Qin
notes: Domain-specific (nutrition) benchmark for evaluating LLMs on carbohydrate estimation from meal descriptions. RAG is tested as one of several prompting strategies but the paper does not address unreliable evidence, retrieval robustness, conflicts, attacks, calibration, or any robust-RAG axis. Out of scope; closest taxonomy is multimodal_agentic_code (domain-specific RAG setting) with evaluation_benchmark as secondary.

title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts
authors: Jihoon Tack; Jaehyung Kim; Eric Mitchell; Jinwoo Shin; Yee Whye Teh; Jonathan Richard Schwarz
notes: MAC proposes an online adaptation framework using amortized context modulations stored in a memory bank to update a frozen LM efficiently. The main contributions are computational/memory efficiency and knowledge retention, not robustness to unreliable evidence. Although the paper briefly notes that retrieved documents may contain counterfactual information and shows MAC can complement RAG (e.g., improving over BM25), it does not analyze, mitigate, or evaluate noisy/adversarial/conflicting evidence in a robust-RAG sense. Treated as background/boundary.

title: Optimizing Retrieval for RAG via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jiawei Zhou; Lei Chen
notes: R3 is a retriever optimization framework using RL with downstream RAG rewards. While it acknowledges the IR-RAG gap (retrievers returning semantically related but unhelpful or misleading content), the core contribution is a training paradigm (reinforced contrastive learning) for better retrieval, not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, robustness, calibration, or security. General RAG improvement work, marginal to the map.

title: Patent Response System Optimised for Faithfulness: Procedural Knowledge Embodiment with Knowledge Graph and Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Language Models (KnowLLM 2024)
notes: Domain-specific RAG+KG system for patent Office Action responses. Although it reports faithfulness improvement across six error types, the contribution is a procedural-knowledge integration pipeline (PPNet KG + PRLLM + RAG) for a patent application, not an analysis or mitigation of unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, conflict, or adversarial corruption. Boundary at most.

title: PlanRAG: A Plan-then-Retrieval Augmented Generation for Generative Large Language Models as Decision Makers
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: PlanRAG proposes iterative plan-then-retrieve RAG for a new Decision QA task on graph/relational DBs, with a DQA benchmark from video games. The contribution is a task-decomposition/planning method and decision-making benchmark, not a study of unreliable evidence (noise, conflicts, attacks, distractors, uncertainty, abstention, calibration). The iterative re-planning loosely resembles adaptive retrieval (calibration_control) but is not framed as a robustness mechanism. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Quebec Automobile Insurance Question-Answering With Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the Natural Legal Language Processing Workshop 2024
notes: Domain-specific (Quebec automobile insurance) RAG application paper. Creates two French corpora and evaluates GPT-4o with RAG, reporting 5-13% factually incorrect answers. While it discusses hallucination/reliability concerns in a critical domain, the contribution is primarily a domain corpus and evaluation, not a generalizable robust RAG method or analysis of unreliable evidence. Falls outside core robust-RAG scope but touches on faithfulness/reliability as boundary context.

title: R$^2$AG: Incorporating Retrieval Information into Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: R2AG proposes an architectural enhancement (R2-Former) to bridge semantic gap between retriever and LLM via retrieval-aware prompting. While the paper mentions low-quality documents and validates 'robustness' as one of its claimed properties, the primary contribution is a general RAG framework improvement rather than a method specifically targeting unreliable evidence, noise handling, or evidence quality control. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval as a secondary motivation, but core contribution is not robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: RAG-HAT: A Hallucination-Aware Tuning Pipeline for LLM in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
notes: RAG-HAT proposes a hallucination-aware tuning pipeline: trains a detection model to identify span-level hallucinations and provide explanations, then uses GPT-4 Turbo to rewrite outputs and applies DPO to fine-tune the generator for improved contextual faithfulness. Maps to knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness to retrieved evidence) with mitigation at the generator. Evaluated on RAGTruth. Not a benchmark contribution itself, but a solid mitigation method for hallucination/unfaithful generation in RAG.

title: RAG-SR: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Neural Symbolic Regression
authors: Hengzhe Zhang; Qi Chen; Bing XUE; Wolfgang Banzhaf; Mengjie Zhang
notes: Domain-specific application of RAG to neural symbolic regression. Uses retrieval to ground LM-generated symbolic trees and reduce hallucination, but contribution is a new SR method, not a study/evaluation/defense of RAG robustness under unreliable evidence. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: RAG-Studio: Towards In-Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation Through Self-Alignment
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Primary contribution is in-domain adaptation of RAG via self-aligned synthetic data and joint fine-tuning of retriever+generator. While the framework does train the LLM with CoT rationale to classify context as helpful/irrelevant/misleading and to withstand noisy contexts (citing Yoran et al., RAFT), this noise-robustness is auxiliary to the main domain-adaptation goal. Not a focused unreliable-evidence/robustness contribution; out of map B core scope but tangential to noisy_retrieval.

title: RAG4GFM: Bridging Knowledge Gaps in Graph Foundation Models through Graph Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Xingliang Wang; Zemin Liu; Junxiao Han; Shuiguang Deng
notes: General graph-RAG framework for Graph Foundation Models proposing multi-level indexing, task-aware retrieval, and graph fusion to improve knowledge updating efficiency and reduce hallucinations. While 'faithful reasoning' is mentioned as motivation, the paper does not analyze unreliable evidence, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflict, calibration, or robustness benchmarks; it is a standard graph-RAG method paper. Closest taxonomy bucket is multimodal_agentic_code (graph-specific RAG), but out of scope for robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence map.

title: RAGLAB: A Modular and Research-Oriented Unified Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
notes: RAGLAB is a modular open-source framework for reproducing and fairly comparing 6 RAG algorithms across 10 benchmarks. It is general RAG infrastructure/tooling without a specific contribution to unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial threat, calibration, or answerability. Closest taxonomy label is evaluation_benchmark due to its fair-comparison and evaluation focus, but it does not target robustness axes.

title: RAGRouter: Learning to Route Queries to Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Jiarui Zhang; Xiangyu Liu; Yong Hu; Chaoyue Niu; Fan Wu; Guihai Chen
notes: Proposes RAGRouter, a contrastive-learning router that selects the best LLM from a pool for each RAG query, modeling document/RAG-capability embeddings. Primary contribution is multi-model routing for performance/efficiency, not handling unreliable evidence. Only a small appendix section (G) touches noisy retrieval. Closest taxonomy fit is calibration_control (system-level model selection decision); secondary noisy_retrieval for the appendix analysis. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: RAGViz: Diagnose and Visualize Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
notes: EMNLP system demonstration paper presenting RAGViz, a visualization/diagnostic tool that displays token- and document-level attention from LLM generation to retrieved passages, with document toggling for side-by-side comparison. It can help users qualitatively distinguish hallucinations stemming from parametric memory vs retrieved (external) memory, which loosely touches on knowledge conflict and document utility. However, the paper does not propose a robustness method, defense, benchmark, calibration mechanism, or quantitative evaluation of unreliable evidence; it is primarily a tool/utility. Treated as background context only.

title: RAPID: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
authors:
Guanzheng Chen, Qilong Feng, Jinjie Ni, Xin Li, Michael Qizhe Shieh;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:8093-8107
notes: RAPID is a long-context inference acceleration method using RAG as a drafter for speculative decoding. The primary contribution is efficiency (throughput speedup) and quality enhancement via knowledge transfer from RAG drafter to long-context target LLM. While the paper briefly mentions 'robustness to retrieval quality' as a side analysis, the work is not about unreliable evidence, noisy retrieval mitigation, calibration, security, or answerability. It is a decoding/efficiency method rather than a robust-RAG contribution, so out of scope.

title: ReFIR: Grounding Large Restoration Models with Retrieval Augmentation
authors: Hang Guo; Tao Dai; Zhihao Ouyang; Taolin Zhang; Yaohua Zha; Bin Chen; Shu-Tao Xia
notes: Applies retrieval augmentation concept to image restoration (LRMs) using retrieved HQ reference images to mitigate visual hallucination. This is a multimodal generative application, not a study of unreliable evidence, robustness, attacks, calibration, or evaluation of robust RAG. Out of scope for Map B.

title: ReMindRAG: Low-Cost LLM-Guided Knowledge Graph Traversal for Efficient RAG
authors: Yikuan Hu; Jifeng Zhu; Lanrui Tang; Chen Huang
notes: KG-RAG system focused on cost efficiency and effectiveness via LLM-guided graph traversal with memory replay. No specific contribution to robustness under unreliable evidence, adversarial threats, calibration, or answerability. Brief mention of reducing 'irrelevant noise' is incidental to the efficiency goal. General RAG method, out of scope.

title: RealRAG: Retrieval-augmented Realistic Image Generation via Self-reflective Contrastive Learning
authors:
Yuanhuiyi Lyu, Xu Zheng, Lutao Jiang, Yibo Yan, Xin Zou, Huiyu Zhou, Linfeng Zhang, Xuming Hu;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:41772-41790
notes: RealRAG is a retrieval-augmented framework for text-to-image generation using self-reflective contrastive learning to retrieve images that compensate for missing knowledge in generative models. Focus is on improving image realism/FID, not on robustness under unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, conflict resolution, calibration, or answerability. General multimodal RAG application without an unreliable-evidence/robustness contribution.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 13th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing and the 3rd Conference of the Asia-Pacific Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: Paper proposes new RAG training objectives (DKS and RAC) using rich answer encoding to capture knowledge-relevant (not just label-relevant) passages on MSMARCO and KILT-WoW. While the word 'robust' appears, the contribution is a general retrieval/training improvement for KIG, not an analysis or mitigation of unreliable evidence, distraction, conflict, adversarial corruption, calibration, or evaluation of robustness. Closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval (false-negative passage problem in training data), but it is out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Retrieval augmented text-to-SQL generation for epidemiological question answering using electronic health records
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 6th Clinical Natural Language Processing Workshop
notes: Domain-specific RAG application for text-to-SQL on EHR/claims data for epidemiological QA. Demonstrates that retrieving similar Q-SQL pairs improves accuracy over static prompting, but provides no contribution on unreliable evidence, robustness, conflict, adversarial attacks, calibration, or answerability. Standard RAG efficacy study in a clinical setting — out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies: Student Research Workshop
notes: NAACL SRW thesis proposal on RAG across heterogeneous knowledge sources (text/tables/KGs) to improve coverage. Briefly notes that scaling to CCNet hurts performance due to lower-quality web content, but the paper's contribution is knowledge integration, not analyzing/mitigating unreliable evidence, distraction, conflict, or adversarial corruption. Out of scope for robust RAG.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation in multilingual settings
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Language Models (KnowLLM 2024)
notes: Paper establishes a multilingual RAG (mRAG) baseline across 13 languages, studying retriever/generator/evaluation components. Primary contribution is a baseline pipeline and analysis of multilingual settings, not a robustness mechanism for unreliable evidence. While it mentions limitations like wrong document reading and irrelevant retrieval, and notes evaluation metric needs adjustment for multilingual settings, these are not the central contributions. Closest taxonomy fit is multimodal_agentic_code (domain-specific RAG setting), but lacks unique robustness mechanism. Useful as background for multilingual RAG context.

title: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: KGI system extends DPR with hard negative mining (mitigates retrieval noise/hard negatives in training) and evaluates domain adaptation (zero/few-shot TACRED). 'Robust' refers to training robustness and domain transfer rather than adversarial/conflicting evidence handling. Boundary support for robust RAG.

title: SeRTS: Self-Rewarding Tree Search for Biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: SeRTS proposes a self-rewarding MCTS-based retrieval method for biomedical RAG to find more relevant documents and PPO-train LLMs. It is a general RAG retrieval improvement in a domain setting; it does not explicitly study unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflict, calibration/abstention, or robustness evaluation. Closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval (improving retrieval quality), but contribution is not centrally about robustness, so out of scope.

title: Self-Retrieval: End-to-End Information Retrieval with One Large Language Model
authors: Qiaoyu Tang; Jiawei Chen; Zhuoqun Li; Bowen Yu; Yaojie Lu; ChengFu; Haiyang Yu; Hongyu Lin; Fei Huang; Ben He; Xianpei Han; Le Sun; Yongbin Li
notes: Proposes Self-Retrieval, a unified end-to-end IR architecture inside a single LLM (indexing/retrieval/reranking via constrained decoding and self-assessment). Evaluated on NQ/TriviaQA/MS MARCO and downstream RAG quality. No contribution on unreliable-evidence robustness, adversarial corruption, noisy/conflicting context handling, calibration, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Superposition Prompting: Improving and Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors:
Thomas Merth, Qichen Fu, Mohammad Rastegari, Mahyar Najibi;
    Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:35507-35527
notes: ICML 2024 paper proposing superposition prompting for RAG. Explicitly addresses the 'distraction phenomenon' where irrelevant retrieved context degrades quality, using path pruning to discard irrelevant documents based on importance metric. Although the main framing is efficiency/acceleration, the path pruning mechanism is a concrete mitigation for distraction in long-context RAG, which makes it relevant to robust RAG. Evaluated on QA benchmarks (NaturalQuestions-Open) with accuracy + speed metrics.

title: TRACE: Grounding Time Series in Context for Multimodal Embedding and Retrieval
authors: Jialin Chen; Ziyu Zhao; Gaukhar Nurbek; Aosong Feng; Ali Maatouk; Leandros Tassiulas; Yifeng Gao; Rex Ying
notes: TRACE is a cross-modal time-series/text retriever for RAG augmentation of time-series foundation models. Its contributions are channel-level alignment and hard negative mining for retrieval quality, plus state-of-the-art encoder performance. It does not study unreliable evidence, noisy/distracting/conflicting/adversarial retrieval, calibration, or answerability for robust RAG. Closest taxonomy is multimodal_agentic_code (multimodal RAG setting), but no specific robustness mechanism — out of scope.

title: Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Domain-specific RAG application: integrates multilingual KG retrieval into NMT for cross-cultural entity translation. Introduces XC-Translate benchmark and KG-MT method, but evaluation is about translation quality (BLEU/COMET/M-ETA), not about unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial corruption, conflict, calibration, or answerability. No contribution to robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Two-tiered Encoder-based Hallucination Detection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Wild
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
notes: Proposes RAGHalu, a two-tiered encoder-based hallucination detector for enterprise RAG that classifies LLM response sentences as VERIFIABLE/NO-INFO then SUPPORTED/UNSUPPORTED against retrieved KB articles. Addresses contextual faithfulness (response vs. evidence) and serves as a guardrail for human-in-the-loop escalation. Also releases re-annotated public dataset. Fits knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness) with secondary control and benchmark aspects. EMNLP Industry Track.

title: Unified Generative and Discriminative Training for Multi-modal Large Language Models
authors: Wei Chow; Juncheng Li; Qifan Yu; Kaihang Pan; Hao Fei; Zhiqi Ge; Shuai Yang; Siliang Tang; Hanwang Zhang; Qianru Sun
notes: Paper proposes a unified generative+discriminative training strategy (Sugar) for MLLMs to improve fine-grained semantic and retrieval performance. RAG is only mentioned as a downstream application enabled by the unified model. No contribution on unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, conflict, adversarial robustness, calibration, or evaluation of robust RAG. Out of scope.

title: WebBrain: Learning to Generate Factually Correct Articles for Queries by Grounding on Large Web Corpus
authors: Hongjin Qian; Yutao Zhu; Zhicheng Dou; Haoqi Gu; Xinyu Zhang; Zheng Liu; Ruofei Lai; Zhao Cao; Jian-Yun Nie; Ji-Rong Wen
notes: Introduces WebBrain task/dataset and ReGen framework for generating factual Wikipedia-style articles grounded on web corpus. Focus is on hallucination reduction via better retrieval+citation+pretraining, not on specific unreliable-evidence robustness (noise analysis, conflict, attacks, calibration). Treated as background grounded-generation benchmark rather than core robust RAG contribution.

title: Chain of Agents: Large Language Models Collaborating on Long-Context Tasks
authors: Yusen Zhang; Ruoxi Sun; Yanfei Chen; Tomas Pfister; Rui Zhang; Sercan O Arik
notes: Proposes Chain-of-Agents multi-agent framework for long-context tasks (QA, summarization, code completion); uses RAG only as a baseline. Touches on 'lost in the middle' long-context focus issue but does not address unreliable evidence, retrieval noise, adversarial corruption, conflict, calibration, or robustness evaluation. General capability/efficiency method for long-context, not robust RAG.

title: ChatQA 2: Bridging the Gap to Proprietary LLMs in Long Context and RAG Capabilities
authors: Peng Xu; Wei Ping; Xianchao Wu; Chejian Xu; Zihan Liu; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
notes: Primarily a capability-building paper for long-context LLM + RAG (extending Llama3 to 128K, training recipe, RAG vs long-context comparison). Mentions robustness to chunk size and analyzes top-k tradeoffs (fragmentation/irrelevance), but these are secondary findings, not focused on unreliable evidence, conflicts, adversarial inputs, calibration, or answerability. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval, but contribution is general RAG/long-context performance.

title: ChatQA: Surpassing GPT-4 on Conversational QA and RAG
authors: Zihan Liu; Wei Ping; Rajarshi Roy; Peng Xu; Chankyu Lee; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
notes: ChatQA's primary contribution is a two-stage instruction tuning recipe to build a strong open conversational QA/RAG model competitive with GPT-4, plus ChatRAG Bench (10 datasets). It briefly addresses unanswerable questions/hallucination avoidance, but this is one of four contributions and not a focused robustness study under unreliable evidence. Treated as background general-RAG capability paper; unanswerable handling gives weak support relevance only.

title: Deliberation on Priors: Trustworthy Reasoning of Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs
authors: Jie Ma; Ning Qu; Zhitao Gao; Xing Rui; Jun Liu; Hongbin Pei; Jiang Xie; Lingyun Song; Pinghui Wang; Jing Tao; su zhou
notes: KG-RAG method (DP) that improves KGQA accuracy via knowledge distillation of structural priors and a reasoning-introspection module that verifies extracted constraints and triggers backtracking. The 'trustworthy' framing is about faithful KG reasoning paths, not handling unreliable/noisy evidence, conflicting sources, adversarial corruption, or answerability. Closest taxonomy label is calibration_control due to introspection/verification with backtracking, but core contribution is a KGQA accuracy method rather than a robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence contribution; out of scope.

title: Do Metadata and Appearance of the Retrieved Webpages Affect LLM's Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 7th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
notes: Studies how non-textual metadata (publication time, source credibility, webpage appearance) affects LLM reasoning when retrieved documents present conflicting evidence. Uses ConflictingQA and introduces ConflictingQA-FAKE. Core knowledge_conflict analysis with implications for adversarial manipulation (acknowledged in ethics). BlackboxNLP workshop at EMNLP 2024.

title: Optimizing LLM Based Retrieval Augmented Generation Pipelines in the Financial Domain
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 6: Industry Track)
notes: NAACL Industry Track financial-domain RAG benchmark. Systematically varies retrieval quality (gold doc presence, number of retrieved docs, ordering) across 6 LLMs and 9 prompts to study impact on answer generation. Explicitly analyzes distractor documents and missing gold doc effects, plus pseudo-helpfulness/hallucination when evidence is missing. Fits noisy_retrieval (retrieval imperfection analysis) with distraction and evaluation_benchmark as secondary. Not a method contribution but useful empirical support.

title: Position: Retrieval-augmented systems can be dangerous medical communicators
authors:
Lionel Wong, Ayman Ali, Raymond M Xiong, Zejiang Shen, Yoon Kim, Monica Agrawal;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:82347-82359
notes: ICML position paper arguing that RAG systems in medicine are 'pragmatically misaligned': even when individual facts are accurate, selective extraction and failure to reason about implicit query presuppositions/biases (e.g., 'why is X dangerous' vs. 'why is X safe', symptoms of disputed conditions) yield misleading outputs. Large-scale query study with LLM-as-judge evaluation. Primary failure framed as ambiguous/underspecified queries with implicit presuppositions (ood_uncertainty); also relates to selective context use (distraction) in a domain-specific (medical) RAG setting. Useful supporting/positioning work rather than a core method or benchmark resource.

title: Reasoning-Enhanced Healthcare Predictions with Knowledge Graph Community Retrieval
authors: Pengcheng Jiang; Cao Xiao; Minhao Jiang; Parminder Bhatia; Taha Kass-Hout; Jimeng Sun; Jiawei Han
notes: KARE is a domain-specific healthcare RAG framework that uses KG community retrieval plus LLM reasoning for mortality/readmission prediction on MIMIC-III/IV. It motivates the work by noting traditional RAG retrieves 'sparse or irrelevant' info, but the core contribution is a new KG-construction + retrieval + fine-tuning pipeline for accuracy on clinical prediction, not an analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, conflict, attack, or calibration. Boundary multimodal/domain-specific RAG application; not core to robust-RAG map.

title: Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 6: Industry Track)
notes: Industry application paper deploying RAG to reduce hallucination in structured JSON workflow generation. Trains a domain-specific retriever and fine-tunes LLM with retrieved context; main contributions are practical (reduced hallucination, smaller LLM footprint, OOD generalization) rather than a robustness/unreliable-evidence analysis. No study of adversarial inputs, knowledge conflicts, calibration, or noisy/distracting retrieval as an explicit research axis. Closest taxonomy fit is noisy_retrieval because of retriever-LLM alignment for entity grounding, but the paper does not analyze retrieval noise per se.

title: SV-RAG: LoRA-Contextualizing Adaptation of  MLLMs for Long Document Understanding
authors: Jian Chen; Ruiyi Zhang; Yufan Zhou; Tong Yu; Franck Dernoncourt; Jiuxiang Gu; Ryan A. Rossi; Changyou Chen; Tong Sun
notes: SV-RAG is a multimodal RAG framework using LoRA-adapted MLLMs for long visually-rich document understanding. Focus is on efficient evidence page retrieval and QA, not on unreliable evidence, robustness, adversarial attacks, conflict, calibration, or answerability. VisR-Bench is a standard QA benchmark without robustness/perturbation axes. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: SearchLVLMs: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Augmenting Large Vision-Language Models by Searching Up-to-Date Internet Knowledge
authors: Chuanhao Li; Zhen Li; Chenchen Jing; Shuo Liu; Wenqi Shao; Yuwei Wu; Ping Luo; Yu Qiao; Kaipeng Zhang
notes: Plug-and-play internet-augmented generation framework for LVLMs to access up-to-date knowledge via search engines. Includes hierarchical website/content filtering and a new UDK-VQA benchmark. The filtering touches on noisy web retrieval, but the paper's primary contribution is enabling multimodal IAG for fresh knowledge rather than analyzing/mitigating unreliable evidence, conflicts, or adversarial corruption. Boundary multimodal RAG application.

title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
authors: Xiaoqian Shen; Wenxuan Zhang; Jun Chen; Mohamed Elhoseiny
notes: Graph-based RAG for long video understanding. Explicitly addresses retrieval noise and distraction by hard-negative retrieved clips via a structured post-retrieval reasoning/verification step. Robustness mechanism is tailored to the video/multimodal setting (graph over clips + structured query decomposition), so multimodal_agentic_code is primary with noisy_retrieval and distraction as secondary. Evaluation is mainly QA accuracy on MLVU/VideoMME/LongVideoBench, not a robustness benchmark per se, hence support rather than core.

title: VimoRAG: Video-based Retrieval-augmented 3D Motion Generation for Motion Language Models
authors: Haidong Xu; Guangwei Xu; Zhedong Zheng; Xiatian Zhu; Wei Ji; Xiangtai Li; Ruijie Guo; Meishan Zhang; Min zhang; Hao Fei
notes: Domain-specific (3D motion generation) cross-modal video-based RAG. Explicitly identifies and addresses error propagation from inaccurate/low-quality retrieved videos via McDPO, which teaches the LLM when to use/ignore noisy retrieved video signals. Robustness contribution is real but secondary to introducing the new motion-RAG paradigm; primary label set to multimodal_agentic_code with noisy_retrieval as secondary. Boundary support evidence for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Visual Haystacks: A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark
authors: Tsung-Han Wu; Giscard Biamby; Jerome Quenum; Ritwik Gupta; Joseph E. Gonzalez; Trevor Darrell; David Chan
notes: Vision-centric NIAH benchmark for multi-image QA; explicitly evaluates visual distractor susceptibility, multi-image reasoning failures, and positional ('lost-in-the-middle') bias in long-context LMMs. Also introduces MIRAGE visual-RAG framework as mitigation. Primary contribution is benchmark; distraction and multimodal RAG robustness are key axes.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shicheng Xu; Liang Pang; Huawei Shen; Xueqi Cheng
notes: ICLR 2025 paper provides theoretical framework decomposing RAG token prediction into benefit (distribution completion) and detriment (distribution contradiction from noisy/incorrect retrieval). Proposes Tok-RAG, a token-level collaborative generation method that decides whether to trust RAG output or pure LLM at each token without training/evaluators. Primary contribution is a control/calibration mechanism for trusting evidence; addresses knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved knowledge and noisy retrieval as underlying failure modes.

title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: ARES is an automated RAG evaluation framework assessing context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance using fine-tuned LLM judges with PPI-based confidence intervals. Core contribution to evaluation of robust RAG, directly addresses faithfulness/hallucination and retrieval quality dimensions. Published at NAACL 2024.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: FLARE proposes active/adaptive retrieval that triggers re-retrieval when LM emits low-confidence tokens during generation, and uses forward-looking next-sentence as query. This is a calibration-based control mechanism for when/what to retrieve (well-calibrated LM probabilities used as a trigger). Also notes that low-confidence tokens can distract retrievers (secondary: distraction). Evaluated on long-form QA and summarization.

title: An Information Bottleneck Perspective for Effective Noise Filtering on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: ACL 2024 long paper. Introduces Information Bottleneck principle to train a noise filter for RAG that compresses retrieved passages, explicitly removing irrelevant/noisy content while preserving info needed for the answer. Handles case where retrieval is irrelevant by compressing to empty. Directly targets unreliable-evidence (noisy retrieval) with defense/mitigation via context-assembly filtering. Evaluated on NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA for correctness and compression rate.

title: Auto-GDA: Automatic Domain Adaptation for Efficient Grounding Verification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Tobias Leemann; Periklis Petridis; Giuseppe Vietri; Dionysis Manousakas; Aaron Roth; Sergul Aydore
notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposing Auto-GDA, an unsupervised synthetic-data domain adaptation framework to train lightweight NLI models for grounding verification (faithfulness checking) of RAG outputs. Directly addresses hallucination/ungrounded generation by enabling efficient post-hoc verification that the answer is supported by retrieved evidence. Primary label is knowledge_conflict (contextual faithfulness); calibration_control is secondary because the verifier supports trust/abstain decisions.

title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
notes: BEIR is a heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark covering 18 datasets across 9 tasks to evaluate OOD generalization of retrievers (lexical, sparse, dense, late-interaction, re-ranking). It is foundational infrastructure for retrieval evaluation but does not study RAG under unreliable evidence (no generator robustness, no conflict/adversarial/distractor analysis at the RAG level). Useful background for retrieval-quality framing but not a core robust-RAG contribution.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
authors: Yangning Li; Yinghui Li; Xinyu Wang; Yong Jiang; Zhen Zhang; Xinran Zheng; Hui Wang; Hai-Tao Zheng; Fei Huang; Jingren Zhou; Philip S. Yu
notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposes Dyn-VQA benchmark (rapidly-changing answers, multimodal, multi-hop questions) and OmniSearch self-adaptive planning agent for multimodal RAG. Addresses rigidity of heuristic mRAG: outdated vs. newer mixed knowledge and overloaded queries. Robustness contribution is in the multimodal agentic setting via adaptive retrieval planning; also serves as benchmark. Primary label set to multimodal_agentic_code since the mechanism is unique to multimodal agentic RAG.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
notes: MIRAGE benchmark + MedRAG toolkit for systematic evaluation of medical RAG across 5 corpora, 4 retrievers, 6 LLMs on 5 medical QA datasets. Primary contribution is finding optimal RAG configurations for medicine. Touches on context-utilization (lost-in-the-middle effect, log-linear scaling) as secondary analysis, but lacks explicit focus on unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, knowledge conflict, or selective answerability. Domain-specific benchmark; boundary context for robust-RAG map.

title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation
authors: Wenbin An; Jiahao Nie; Feng Tian; Haonan Lin; mingxiang cai; Yaqiang Wu; QianYing Wang; Xiaoqin Zhang; Shijian Lu
notes: ALFAR explicitly targets two robust-RAG issues in MRAG: (1) knowledge conflicts between parametric and retrieved contextual knowledge, and (2) attention bias diluting relevant context tokens. Training-free, plug-and-play generator-side method using adaptive logits fusion and attention reallocation. Shows robustness across varying contextual-knowledge quality (including noisy retrievals). Multimodal-specific but addresses core unreliable-evidence concerns.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Liang Wang; Haonan Chen; Nan Yang; Xiaolong Huang; Zhicheng Dou; Furu Wei
notes: CoRAG trains LLMs to iteratively retrieve and reformulate queries, dynamically deciding next retrieval action based on state. Addresses imperfect single-step retrieval and reports robustness across retrievers of varying quality. Primary contribution is adaptive/iterative retrieval (calibration_control); secondary touches noisy retrieval mitigation. Not focused on adversarial or unanswerable settings, hence support-level.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
authors: Manuel Faysse; Hugues Sibille; Tony Wu; Bilel Omrani; Gautier Viaud; CELINE HUDELOT; Pierre Colombo
notes: ColPali introduces a vision-language document retrieval method and the ViDoRe benchmark for visually rich document retrieval. The contribution is about retrieval efficiency/quality on visual documents for downstream RAG, not about unreliable evidence, robustness, conflict, adversarial corruption, calibration, or answerability. Benchmark evaluates standard retrieval utility, no perturbation/threat axis. Closest taxonomy label is multimodal_agentic_code (multimodal RAG setting) but no robustness mechanism specific to the setting; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: DRAGIN is a dynamic/adaptive RAG framework that decides WHEN to retrieve (via token entropy + self-attention importance via RIND) and WHAT to retrieve (via QFS over full context). Explicit motivation includes avoiding unnecessary retrieval that 'may introduce irrelevant or noisy data to LLMs which could jeopardize the quality of the outputs.' Fits calibration_control (adaptive retrieval / selective triggering). Secondary tie to noisy_retrieval as a motivation. ACL long paper; useful support for the calibration axis of robust RAG.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Wenxuan Shi; Haochen Tan; Chuqiao Kuang; Xiaoguang Li; Hanting Chen; Xiaozhe Ren; Yasheng Wang; Lu Hou; Lifeng Shang
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper introducing DeepDiver (RL framework for adaptive Search Intensity Scaling) and WebPuzzle benchmark. Explicitly targets real-web noisy/conflicting/unreliable sources and frames four behaviors: evidence gathering, conflict resolution, verification & denoising, reflection & correction. Primary contribution is adaptive when/how-much-to-retrieve decision-making (calibration_control); secondary contributions touch noisy retrieval, knowledge conflicts, and benchmark construction. Not a pure robustness paper but provides clear support evidence.

title: Do You Know What You Are Talking About? Characterizing Query-Knowledge Relevance For Reliable Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: EMNLP 2024 paper that proposes a statistical (goodness-of-fit) framework to detect out-of-knowledge queries (online) and query distribution shifts (offline) for reliable RAG. Directly addresses answerability/OOK detection and selective abstention, strong fit for ood_uncertainty with calibration_control secondary.

title: Follow My Instruction and Spill the Beans: Scalable Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Zhenting Qi; Hanlin Zhang; Eric P. Xing; Sham M. Kakade; Himabindu Lakkaraju
notes: ICLR 2025 paper on prompt-injection data extraction attacks against RIC-based RAG systems. Demonstrates datastore leakage across many instruction-tuned LMs (Llama2, Mistral, Vicuna, etc.) and production GPTs; also explores position-bias mitigation as defense. Clear adversarial corruption threat model with attack+light defense; primary contribution is attack methodology and evaluation.

title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
authors:
Bernal Jiménez Gutiérrez, Yiheng Shu, Weijian Qi, Sizhe Zhou, Yu Su;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:21497-21515
notes: HippoRAG 2 is a general RAG architecture improvement using KG + Personalized PageRank for non-parametric continual learning across factual, sense-making, and multi-hop QA. While it briefly notes that LLM-generated summarization noise hurts retrieval corpora, the paper's main contribution is a better retrieval/memory framework rather than handling unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflict, calibration, or abstention. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering
authors: Xiaoxin He; Yijun Tian; Yifei Sun; Nitesh V Chawla; Thomas Laurent; Yann LeCun; Xavier Bresson; Bryan Hooi
notes: General RAG method for textual graphs (PCST-based subgraph retrieval) plus a GraphQA benchmark. Mentions hallucination mitigation but in the standard sense (retrieving relevant subgraph instead of hallucinating nodes/edges), not in the robust-RAG-under-unreliable-evidence sense. No analysis of noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence, calibration, or answerability. Domain-specific (graph) RAG application, marginal to the map.

title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Linhao Luo; Zicheng Zhao; Gholamreza Haffari; Dinh Phung; Chen Gong; Shirui Pan
notes: Graph foundation model for RAG focused on multi-hop retrieval via GNN over KG-index. Briefly motivates by graph noise/incompleteness, but the contribution is a general retrieval method (scaling, generalization), not an unreliable-evidence robustness, calibration, or attack/defense study. Closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval but the paper lacks explicit robustness analysis under noisy or unreliable evidence. Out of scope.

title: Generate-then-Ground in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-hop Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: ACL 2024 paper proposing GenGround framework for multi-hop QA. Explicitly motivated by noise in retrieved documents and the limitation of retriever performance. Generates answers from parametric knowledge first, then grounds in retrieved documents to revise. Addresses both noisy retrieval (primary) and parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge tension (secondary). Mitigation-oriented architectural change in the RAG pipeline.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
authors: Bernal Jimenez Gutierrez; Yiheng Shu; Yu Gu; Michihiro Yasunaga; Yu Su
notes: HippoRAG is a neurobiologically-inspired RAG framework using knowledge graphs and Personalized PageRank to enable single-step multi-hop retrieval. Focus is on knowledge integration efficiency and multi-hop QA performance (MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA), not on robustness to unreliable evidence, noise analysis, adversarial attacks, conflicts, calibration, or answerability. It is a general RAG architecture/efficiency contribution, out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Influence Guided Context Selection for Effective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiale Deng; Yanyan Shen; Ziyuan Pei; Youmin Chen; Linpeng Huang
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper proposing Contextual Influence (CI) value and a surrogate model (CSM) to filter poor-quality/irrelevant/redundant retrieved contexts. Directly targets noisy retrieval robustness; also touches distraction (negative marginal contexts) and parametric-vs-context redundancy/conflict (generator-aware metric). Clear defense/mitigation at context assembly stage.

title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
authors: Zhepei Wei; Wei-Lin Chen; Yu Meng
notes: ICLR 2025 paper explicitly targets imperfect retrievers and noisy corpora. Proposes InstructRAG: LM learns explicit denoising via self-synthesized rationales (ICL or SFT). Tested on 5 knowledge-intensive benchmarks with robustness analysis against increased noise ratios and OOD generalization. Clear robust-RAG / noisy retrieval mitigation contribution.

title: LaRA: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Long-Context LLMs – No Silver Bullet for LC or RAG Routing
authors:
Kuan Li, Liwen Zhang, Yong Jiang, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Shuai Wang, Minhao Cheng;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:36846-36867
notes: ICML benchmark (LaRA, 2326 test cases) systematically comparing RAG vs long-context LLMs across model size, context length, task type. Includes hallucination-detection task and 'lost in the middle' analysis showing RAG is more robust to answer position, which is relevant to distraction/context-utilization robustness. Primary contribution is RAG-vs-LC routing rather than unreliable-evidence mitigation, hence boundary support.

title: LongRAG: A Dual-Perspective Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigm for Long-Context Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: LongRAG explicitly targets two RAG failure modes in long-context QA: (1) low-quality/noisy retrieval where substantial noise hinders identification of factual details, and (2) lost-in-the-middle distraction. It proposes a CoT-guided filter and information extractor as mitigations. Relevant to noisy_retrieval with distraction as secondary; EMNLP 2024 main paper.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
notes: Foundational TACL 2024 analysis showing U-shaped performance curve when relevant info is positioned in the middle of long contexts. Directly relevant to RAG distraction/context-utilization: shows that adding more retrieved documents (including distractors) degrades performance and that position of relevant evidence within context matters. Includes case study with retriever-reader on open-domain QA showing model performance saturates before retriever recall.

title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision Language Models
authors: Peng Xia; Kangyu Zhu; Haoran Li; Tianze Wang; Weijia Shi; Sheng Wang; Linjun Zhang; James Zou; Huaxiu Yao
notes: ICLR 2025 multimodal medical RAG system. Robustness contributions include (1) domain-aware retriever selection across radiology/pathology/ophthalmology, (2) adaptive k selection using similarity scores to filter low-quality retrieved contexts, and (3) preference fine-tuning to mitigate cross-modality misalignment and avoid interference from irrelevant retrieved info. Primary label is multimodal_agentic_code since mechanisms are tailored to multimodal medical setting; secondary covers calibration of retrieval, noisy retrieval filtering, and distraction by irrelevant contexts.

title: Measuring and Enhancing Trustworthiness of LLMs in RAG through Grounded Attributions and Learning to Refuse
authors: Maojia Song; Shang Hong Sim; Rishabh Bhardwaj; Hai Leong Chieu; Navonil Majumder; Soujanya Poria
notes: Introduces TRUST-SCORE metric and TRUST-ALIGN DPO-based alignment to improve LLM groundedness in RAG: correctly refusing when documents are insufficient, providing supported citations, and answering only from retrieved evidence. Directly addresses abstention/answerability and faithfulness under potentially insufficient evidence.

title: Model Internals-based Answer Attribution for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: MIRAGE uses model internals (gradient-based saliency) for faithful answer attribution in RAG, addressing contextual faithfulness (whether retrieved docs actually influenced generation vs parametric memory). Closest fit is knowledge_conflict per taxonomy definition mentioning 'contextual faithfulness'. Supports trustworthy RAG but not directly about handling unreliable evidence. EMNLP 2024 main.

title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: MuRAG proposes a multimodal retrieval-augmented transformer for open QA over images and text. The contribution is a new multimodal RAG architecture/training recipe, not robustness to unreliable evidence. Distractor setting is standard QA eval, not a robustness study. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence; treat as foundational multimodal RAG background.

title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
authors:
Chenyang Zhang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jian Lou, Kai Wu, Zilong Wang, Xiaofeng Chen;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:76811-76830
notes: First knowledge poisoning attack on Vision-Language RAG systems; injects a single poison image-text pair into the multimodal knowledge database to manipulate VLRAG responses. Clear adversarial corruption contribution at ICML 2025; secondary label multimodal_agentic_code reflects the VLRAG setting.

title: Provence: efficient and robust context pruning for retrieval-augmented generation
authors: Nadezhda Chirkova; Thibault Formal; Vassilina Nikoulina; Stéphane CLINCHANT
notes: Provence is a sentence-level extractive context pruner that dynamically removes irrelevant retrieved sentences (from zero to all) before LLM generation, explicitly motivated by mitigating propagation of irrelevant retrieved information. Tested for robustness across domains and varying context lengths. Fits noisy_retrieval (removing irrelevant passages) with distraction as secondary (reducing distractor influence on generation). ICLR 2025 venue backbone.

title: RAG-DDR: Optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Differentiable Data Rewards
authors: Xinze Li; Sen Mei; Zhenghao Liu; Yukun Yan; Shuo Wang; Shi Yu; Zheni Zeng; Hao Chen; Ge Yu; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun; Chenyan Xiong
notes: ICLR'25 RAG optimization via DPO with rollout rewards over a two-agent (knowledge refinement + generation) RAG system. Explicitly motivated by knowledge conflict between parametric memory and external knowledge; also reports generalization to noisy documents during generation. Primary contribution is an end-to-end training/optimization method, but robustness to noisy/conflicting evidence is a stated outcome, so support-level inclusion with knowledge_conflict primary and noisy_retrieval secondary.

title: RAG-QA Arena: Evaluating Domain Robustness for Long-form Retrieval Augmented Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: EMNLP 2024 paper introducing LFRQA dataset (long-form answers across 7 domains) and RAG-QA Arena LLM-based evaluation framework specifically targeting cross-domain/OOD robustness of RAG-QA systems. Benchmark for domain robustness evaluation rather than direct unreliable-evidence mitigation, but fits evaluation_benchmark with ood_uncertainty secondary.

title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: System Demonstrations
notes: RAGAs introduces a reference-free automated evaluation framework with three metrics: faithfulness (grounding in context), answer relevance, and context relevance. Directly supports robustness evaluation of RAG systems, particularly faithfulness assessment and detection of irrelevant retrieved context. EACL demo venue.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
authors:
Jennifer Hsia, Afreen Shaikh, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Graham Neubig;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:24139-24155
notes: ICML 2025 paper introducing RAGGED framework with new RSS (stability) and RSC (scalability) metrics to systematically evaluate RAG across retrieval depths. Explicitly analyzes reader robustness to noise as key determinant of RAG effectiveness; directly addresses unreliable retrieval evidence and distractor sensitivity.

title: RAGraph: A General Retrieval-Augmented Graph Learning Framework
authors: Xinke Jiang; Rihong Qiu; Yongxin Xu; WentaoZhang; Yichen Zhu; Ruizhe zhang; Yuchen Fang; Xu Chu; Junfeng Zhao; Yasha Wang
notes: General retrieval-augmented framework for GNNs to improve cross-task/cross-dataset generalization via toy-graph retrieval and prompt-based message passing. No analysis of unreliable evidence, adversarial corruption, conflicts, calibration, or robustness evaluation. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: EMNLP 2024 paper proposing RE-RAG with a Relevance Estimator that produces confidence over retrieved contexts. Confidence is used for reranking, abstention ('unanswerable'), and falling back to parametric knowledge when context is irrelevant—core calibration/control contribution against noisy/distracting retrieval. Intervention spans context assembly (reranking) and system control (decoding strategy).

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Context Compression and Selective Augmentation
authors: Fangyuan Xu; Weijia Shi; Eunsol Choi
notes: RECOMP compresses retrieved documents via extractive/abstractive summarizers and supports selective augmentation (empty summary when documents are irrelevant). Primary motivation is efficiency, but it explicitly mitigates distraction from irrelevant retrieved content and adds a control mechanism for when to use retrieval, so it provides useful support for robust RAG.
