title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
authors: Yue Yu; Wei Ping; Zihan Liu; Boxin Wang; Jiaxuan You; Chao Zhang; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
notes: RankRAG unifies LLM-based reranking with answer generation. Explicitly analyzes top-k trade-off where larger k introduces irrelevant/noisy context that misleads generation (Fig.1), and proposes reranking to filter irrelevant contexts. Primarily a general RAG performance method, but mitigates noisy retrieval via context assembly. Borderline core/support; coded as support since unreliable-evidence handling is motivation but not the central robustness claim.

title: ReDeEP: Detecting Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Mechanistic Interpretability
authors: ZhongXiang Sun; Xiaoxue Zang; Kai Zheng; Jun Xu; Xiao Zhang; Weijie Yu; Yang Song; Han Li
notes: ICLR 2025 paper. Proposes ReDeEP for detecting RAG hallucinations (where retrieved context is accurate but generation conflicts with it) via mechanistic interpretability, decoupling FFN-based parametric knowledge and attention-based external context utilization. Also introduces AARF mitigation method. Core knowledge_conflict between parametric and external knowledge in RAG; secondary calibration_control since it provides detection signal for trust/abstain decisions.

title: ReEval: Automatic Hallucination Evaluation for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Transferable Adversarial Attacks
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2024
notes: ReEval is a dynamic evaluation framework that perturbs evidence via answer swapping and context enriching to test whether retrieval-augmented LLMs faithfully use provided evidence or hallucinate. Although framed as adversarial attacks, the primary contribution is an evaluation methodology for RAG faithfulness; secondary aspects include induced knowledge conflict between parametric memory and perturbed evidence, and adversarial test-case generation with transferability.

title: Reliable Decision‑Making via Calibration‑Oriented Retrieval‑Augmented Generation
authors: Chaeyun Jang; Deukhwan Cho; Seanie Lee; Hyungi Lee; Juho Lee
notes: CalibRAG explicitly targets RAG overconfidence when retrieved documents are irrelevant/distracting. Proposes a forecasting function to predict decision correctness and rerank documents by decision confidence rather than relevance, producing calibrated confidence scores. Core calibration_control contribution; secondary touches on distraction (irrelevant docs misleading LLM) and noisy_retrieval (top-1 hit not optimal). Evaluated via ECE and accuracy on NaturalQA and other datasets. Intervention spans reranking (context assembly) and confidence output (system control).

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
notes: Comparative study of RAG vs long-context LLMs with a self-reflection-based routing hybrid (Self-Route) aimed primarily at cost efficiency, not robustness under unreliable evidence. The routing has some calibration/adaptive-retrieval flavor and the paper discusses RAG failure patterns, but the main contribution is performance/cost trade-off rather than handling noisy, adversarial, or conflicting evidence. Boundary context at best.

title: Retrieval Augmented Visual Question Answering with Outside Knowledge
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Multimodal RAG application for OK-VQA proposing joint training of DPR retriever and answer generator. Briefly notes pseudo-relevance labels can encourage retrieval of misleading documents, but the main contribution is end-to-end training to improve VQA accuracy, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence study. Boundary multimodal RAG context, not core to robust-RAG map.

title: Retrieval is Not Enough: Enhancing RAG through Test-Time Critique and Optimization
authors: Jiaqi Wei; Hao Zhou; Xiang Zhang; Di Zhang; Zijie Qiu; Noah Wei; Jinzhe Li; Wanli Ouyang; Siqi Sun
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper proposing AlignRAG, a test-time critique-driven alignment framework that trains a Critic LM to detect and correct 'reasoning misalignment' (divergence between LLM reasoning and retrieved evidence). Core contribution targets contextual faithfulness of generation to retrieved evidence and explicitly tests robustness under noisy retrieval scenarios. Generator-side mitigation via iterative critique with auto-stopping variant.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis; Ethan Perez; Aleksandara Piktus; Fabio Petroni; Vladimir Karpukhin; Naman Goyal; Heinrich Küttler; Mike Lewis; Wen-tau Yih; Tim Rocktäschel; Sebastian Riedel; Douwe Kiela
notes: Foundational Lewis et al. 2020 RAG paper. Introduces the RAG framework (DPR + BART, end-to-end fine-tuning) and evaluates on open-domain QA, MS-MARCO, Jeopardy, FEVER. No explicit treatment of unreliable evidence, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflict, calibration, or answerability. Serves as background/foundation for the map but is not itself a robust-RAG contribution.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Perception: High-resolution Image Perception Meets Visual RAG
authors:
Wenbin Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Liang Ding, Yingjie Wang, Li Shen, Yong Luo, Bo Du, Dacheng Tao;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:63290-63307
notes: Visual RAG applied to high-resolution image perception in MLLMs. Proposes Spatial-Awareness Layout for retrieved crops and RE-Search that adapts crop count based on model confidence/retrieval scores. Primary contribution is improving HR perception, not addressing unreliable evidence, adversarial attacks, knowledge conflicts, or robustness per se. The confidence-driven crop selection has minor calibration flavor but the paper is a multimodal RAG application; out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: Retrieving, Rethinking and Revising: The Chain-of-Verification Can Improve Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: CoV-RAG introduces a verification module that scores reference and answer quality, judges correctness, and triggers query revision/re-retrieval when needed. Core mechanism is calibrated decision-making (verify→judge→re-retrieve) addressing both external retrieval errors and internal generation hallucinations. Secondary labels cover the retrieval noise correction and conflict between parametric/retrieved knowledge it targets. Findings EMNLP 2024.

title: SEER: Self-Aligned Evidence Extraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: SEER proposes a self-aligned evidence extractor that filters distracting content from retrieved passages, framing the problem as separating supporting vs. distracting content. Uses faithfulness/helpfulness/conciseness experts. Directly addresses distraction and noisy retrieval as defense/mitigation at context-assembly stage. EMNLP 2024 main.

title: SePer: Measure Retrieval Utility Through The Lens Of Semantic Perplexity Reduction
authors: Lu Dai; Yijie Xu; Jinhui Ye; Hao Liu; Hui Xiong
notes: Introduces SePer, a semantic-perplexity-reduction metric to quantify per-retrieval utility in RAG (knowledge gain to the LLM). Not directly about adversarial/unreliable evidence, but provides an evaluation tool that can flag low/zero-utility (irrelevant or distracting) retrievals, which is adjacent to noisy_retrieval and retrieval-quality assessment. Boundary support paper from ICLR 2025.

title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: General RAG best-practices study that systematically compares modules (query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization) for performance/efficiency tradeoffs. Does not focus on unreliable evidence, adversarial robustness, knowledge conflict, distraction, or calibration. Useful as background context on RAG workflow only.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
authors: Akari Asai; Zeqiu Wu; Yizhong Wang; Avirup Sil; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
notes: Self-RAG introduces reflection tokens enabling on-demand retrieval, relevance assessment (IsRel), support evaluation (IsSup), and utility scoring (IsUse). Core contribution is adaptive/selective retrieval with self-critique to handle unreliable or unnecessary evidence, directly addressing calibration and trust control in RAG. ICLR 2024 backbone paper for adaptive RAG.

title: Simple is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Mufei Li; Siqi Miao; Pan Li
notes: SubgraphRAG is a KG-based RAG method focused on efficient and effective subgraph retrieval for KGQA (WebQSP, CWQ). It mentions reducing hallucinations and pruning irrelevant info ('lost in the middle'), but the core contribution is a lightweight MLP retriever with parallel triple scoring, not a robustness/unreliable-evidence/calibration/security mechanism. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence; closest taxonomy label is noisy_retrieval due to relevance filtering, with KG-RAG setting noted as secondary.

title: SmartRAG: Jointly Learn RAG-Related Tasks From the Environment Feedback
authors: Jingsheng Gao; Linxu Li; Ke Ji; Weiyuan Li; Yixin Lian; yuzhuo fu; Bin Dai
notes: SmartRAG jointly optimizes policy network and retriever via PPO. Policy decides when to retrieve, what to query, and when to answer directly — this is adaptive retrieval / decision-making, fitting calibration_control. Not focused on adversarial or noisy evidence robustness, but the 'when to retrieve' decision and reward design (minimize retrieval cost while answering correctly) places it as support-level in the unreliable-evidence map.

title: Speculative RAG: Enhancing Retrieval Augmented Generation through Drafting
authors: Zilong Wang; Zifeng Wang; Long Le; Steven Zheng; Swaroop Mishra; Vincent Perot; Yuwei Zhang; Anush Mattapalli; Ankur Taly; Jingbo Shang; Chen-Yu Lee; Tomas Pfister
notes: Speculative RAG is primarily an efficiency/accuracy framework that uses a smaller specialist drafter and a generalist verifier over diverse document subsets. It mentions mitigating position bias and lost-in-the-middle as side benefits, but the main contribution is the draft-then-verify architecture, not an explicit unreliable-evidence, robustness, attack/defense, or calibration mechanism. Closest taxonomy fit is distraction due to long-context/position-bias framing, but it is not the paper's focus.

title: StructRAG: Boosting Knowledge Intensive Reasoning of LLMs via Inference-time Hybrid Information Structurization
authors: Zhuoqun Li; Xuanang Chen; Haiyang Yu; Hongyu Lin; Yaojie Lu; Qiaoyu Tang; Fei Huang; Xianpei Han; Le Sun; Yongbin Li
notes: StructRAG proposes hybrid information structurization (router + structurizer + utilizer) to convert scattered raw documents into structured knowledge (table/graph/etc.) for knowledge-intensive reasoning. Noise of retrieved chunks is mentioned as motivation, but the primary contribution is a reasoning-enhancement framework for knowledge-intensive QA rather than explicit analysis/mitigation of unreliable evidence, conflict, attack, or calibration. Treated as general RAG method, out of scope.

title: TRACE the Evidence: Constructing Knowledge-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: TRACE explicitly addresses retriever imperfections and irrelevant/noisy documents in multi-hop QA by constructing knowledge-grounded reasoning chains (KG triples) as filtered context. The motivation is mitigation of retrieval noise that degrades RAG performance, especially distracting effect on multi-hop reasoning. Method-side defense via context assembly/restructuring; evaluated on EM/F1 over HotpotQA-style benchmarks.

title: TableRAG: Million-Token Table Understanding with Language Models
authors: Si-An Chen; Lesly Miculicich; Julian Martin Eisenschlos; Zifeng Wang; Zilong Wang; Yanfei Chen; Yasuhisa Fujii; Hsuan-Tien Lin; Chen-Yu Lee; Tomas Pfister
notes: TableRAG is a scalability/efficiency-oriented RAG framework for million-token table understanding via schema+cell retrieval and query expansion. It motivates the work partly via Lost-in-the-Middle (long-context distraction), but the contribution is not an analysis or mitigation of unreliable/noisy/conflicting/adversarial evidence; it is a general structured-data RAG application with new scale benchmarks. Out of scope for robust RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: The Good and The Bad: Exploring Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
notes: Privacy attack on RAG: proposes composite structured prompting to extract private retrieval-database data (targeted/untargeted PII extraction) and studies how retrieval augmentation affects LLM training-data memorization. Adversarial threat to RAG (privacy axis rather than answer manipulation), ACL Findings 2024. Fits adversarial_corruption as primary; also contributes attack benchmark/protocol.

title: Think-on-Graph 2.0: Deep and Faithful Large Language Model Reasoning with Knowledge-guided Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Shengjie Ma; Chengjin Xu; Xuhui Jiang; Muzhi Li; Huaren Qu; Cehao Yang; Jiaxin Mao; Jian Guo
notes: ToG-2 is a hybrid KG+text RAG method using tight-coupling iterative retrieval to improve reasoning depth and reduce hallucinations on complex multi-hop QA. While it mentions 'faithful reasoning' and tests on AdvHotpotQA, the primary contribution is a general retrieval/reasoning enhancement, not explicit analysis or mitigation of unreliable evidence (noise, conflict, attack, abstention). Treated as background for hybrid RAG context.

title: Training Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering through Backtracking Correction
authors: Huawen Feng; ZekunYao; Junhao Zheng; Qianli Ma
notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposing Backtracking Correction, a training method to improve RAG robustness against noisy/irrelevant retrieved documents. Reformulates RAG as multi-step decision-making where the model learns to assess document relevance step-by-step. Core contribution targets noise robustness in retrieval; secondary aspects include handling distractors and decision-making about when to trust evidence.

title: Trustworthy Alignment of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
authors:
Zongmeng Zhang, Yufeng Shi, Jinhua Zhu, Wengang Zhou, Xiang Qi, Peng Zhang, Houqiang Li;
    Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:59827-59850
notes: ICML 2024 paper directly addresses knowledge conflict between parametric and contextual knowledge in RAG. Proposes TRUSTWORTHY-ALIGNMENT, an RL-based method to align retrieval-augmented LLMs to rely on contextual evidence over parametric memory. Evaluates via counterfactual entity substitution. Core contribution to robust RAG under unreliable/conflicting evidence.

title: Understanding Parametric and Contextual Knowledge Reconciliation within Large Language Models
authors: Jun Zhao; Yongzhuo Yang; Xiang Hu; Jingqi Tong; Yi Lu; Wei Wu; Tao Gui; Qi Zhang; Xuanjing Huang
notes: NeurIPS 2025 mechanistic analysis paper using entity-aware probing to trace how LLMs internally reconcile conflicting parametric vs. contextual knowledge in RAG. Directly addresses knowledge conflict mechanisms (attention competition vs. MLP arbitration hypotheses). Analysis paper rather than defense/attack; informs understanding of context vs. parametric integration in robust RAG.

title: Unified Active Retrieval for Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Proposes Unified Active Retrieval (UAR) framework with four orthogonal criteria (intent-, knowledge-, time-sensitive-, self-aware) to decide when to retrieve, addressing the problem that always-on retrieval hurts when irrelevant evidence is fetched. Introduces AR-Bench for evaluating retrieval timing accuracy. Clear calibration/adaptive-retrieval contribution; secondary touches on uncertainty (self-awareness) and acknowledging noisy retrieval harm.

title: Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: ACL 2024 paper proposing INFO-RAG, an unsupervised training method that makes LLMs robust to varied-quality retrieved texts. Explicitly addresses three scenarios: complete/concise retrieval, incomplete/incorrect retrieval (requiring verification and correction with parametric knowledge), and irrelevant retrieval. Directly targets unreliable evidence and demonstrates robustness improvements; defense at the generator side.

title: VRAG-RL: Empower Vision-Perception-Based RAG for Visually Rich Information Understanding via Iterative Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Qiuchen Wang; Ruixue Ding; Yu Zeng; Zehui Chen; Lin Chen; Shihang Wang; Pengjun Xie; Fei Huang; Feng Zhao
notes: Vision-based RAG framework using RL with visual perception action space (crop/zoom) and a reward integrating retrieval NDCG and outcome correctness. Focus is on improving multimodal RAG performance on visually rich documents, not on robustness to unreliable evidence, conflicts, attacks, calibration, or answerability. Mentions of irrelevant retrievals as noise are only motivational, not a robustness contribution. General multimodal RAG application/method.

title: xRAG: Extreme Context Compression for Retrieval-augmented Generation with One Token
authors: Xin Cheng; Xun Wang; Xingxing Zhang; Tao Ge; Si-Qing Chen; Furu Wei; Huishuai Zhang; Dongyan Zhao
notes: xRAG is a context-compression / efficiency method for RAG using modality fusion to project document embeddings into the LLM space. It targets inference cost and context length, not unreliable evidence, robustness, noise/distraction, conflict, adversarial corruption, calibration, or answerability. No robustness contribution; primary_failure_type chosen only as closest stretch (compression interacts with retrieved evidence), but paper is out of scope for the robust-RAG map.
